By Mike Allen · Aug 27, 2026

🍻 Happy Friday Jr! Today's newsletter, edited by Alex Fitzpatrick, is 698 words, a 2½-min. read. Thanks to Sheryl Miller for copy editing.

🚨 Breaking: President Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake America." It's unclear whether he has the authority to rename a body of water shared between countries, as he did last year when he signed a similar order changing the Gulf of Mexico to "Gulf of America." Go deeper.

⚡️ Situational awareness: Trump told Axios in a phone interview today that he isn't concerned that Russia will attack NATO countries.

  • Several media outlets reported that CIA Director John Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow this week was an effort to warn Russia not to attack a NATO country. But Trump disputed those reports: "I am not concerned ... at all. There is no problem." More from Barak Ravid.
 
 
1 big thing: Dire cyberthreat warning
 
Illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios

OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft and more than 100 other companies warned today there's only months to prepare for AI-enabled cyberattacks, Axios' Sam Sabin reports.

  • Hospitals, water treatment plants and other critical infrastructure will face a swarm of hacking threats as AI makes sophisticated cyber capabilities cheaper and more accessible, the group writes in an open letter. (Read.)

🛡️ The group is calling for "collective action," and urges organizations to secure critical infrastructure.

  • Signatories include a range of cloud providers, cybersecurity companies, AI companies, telecoms and financial services companies, and think tanks.

The organizations lay out a plan for how all companies and governments, as well as cybersecurity and AI companies, need to adapt.

  • Organizations need to raise their internal security standards and fix their "highest-risk weaknesses," the group says. They also should "raise the security bar for what you buy, build, and deploy, including AI-generated code."

🤖 Cybersecurity and tech companies must quickly test and build out tools that make "AI-powered defense accessible and deployable for critical-infrastructure operators."

  • Governments need to strengthen channels for sharing actionable threat intelligence, coordinate defense at the local, national and international levels, and fund cyber defense.
  • Frontier AI companies should give defenders access to their most capable response models during major cyber incidents, along with "significant funding, training, and hands-on support."

👾 The letter comes amid a wave of cyberattacks against critical infrastructure, including one targeting U.S. water systems with an apparent AI-generated script.

  • The signatories didn't make any commitments, deadlines or specific investments.

Go deeper.
 
 
2. 🌙 Partial eclipse tonight
 
Graphic: NASA

Most of the U.S. will be treated to a partial lunar eclipse overnight as the Moon passes into Earth's shadow.

  • The result: The Moon will look coppery red, with a thin sliver left partially illuminated.

🌒 The phenomenon peaks just after midnight Eastern Time, when about 96% of the Moon will fall into shadow.

  • Go deeper ... Livestream.
 
 
3. ⚡️ Catch me up
 
A resident walks along a muddy road today following flash floods in Trishuli, Nepal. Photo: Ezra Acayan/Getty Images
  1. 🇳🇵🇨🇳 The death toll from catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-China border has reached more than 350, with over 1,300 people still missing. Get the latest.
  2. 🛢️ The Trump administration is in talks with Venezuela's interim government about taking an ownership stake in the South American country's enormous oil resources. More from Axios' Marc Caputo.
  3. 🇮🇷 Meta removed a network of Facebook and Instagram accounts tied to an Iran-based operation that used AI to target U.S. audiences with posts about American politics, Axios' Sam Sabin is first to report. Go deeper.
  4. 🎤 Dolly Parton left behind plans for decades of posthumous releases, Axios Nashville's Adam Tamburin reports. Longtime manager Danny Nozell said: "Dolly worked up until the day she died." Keep reading.
 
 
4. 🤖 1 fun thing: Meet Microduck
 
Image: Microduck

Tech company Hugging Face today unveiled "Microduck," a small duck-like robot that waddles and picks up small objects in its "beak," Axios' Ina Fried reports.

  • The move is an effort to put a friendly, approachable face on a robotics field dominated by attack dogs and humanoids.

The $399 Microduck comes in several colors and has many sensors, including an eye-like camera, speaker, microphone, WiFi, Bluetooth and even a small lidar sensor.

  • It will come with several preset behaviors, like following a laser pointer.
  • In sample videos, Microduck was also shown picking up a dirty sock, rollerblading, and recovering from falls and efforts to push it off balance.

The target audience: AI developers who can teach the robot new tricks.
